title: Dual side-by-side simulation on two different tracks (one with a 'loop')
description: Run two races at once on two DIFFERENT tracks, each with its own animation + metrics (time, 'where did your speed go?', why) and ideally a head-to-head comparison. Spun off from 0003-web-front-end (done) which provides the Pyodide bridge, present.py, animator and result panel to build on. User specifically asked for a second track 'with a loop in it'. FEASIBILITY FLAG for planning: the 0001 engine is a pure gravity-descent model (Track = ramp angle 0-90 -> transition -> flat, angle monotonically decreasing to 0) and CANNOT represent a vertical loop (no climbing/inversion/centripetal/fall-off physics); a faked loop over flat-track physics would teach wrong physics, violating the app's hard educational-accuracy rule. The engine IS parameterized for different REAL tracks and simulate()/present() already accept an arbitrary track, so a faithful dual race on two engine-valid geometries is buildable now without engine changes. OPEN QUESTIONS for the planning session (do not resolve yet): (1) true vertical loop [needs a big 0001 engine extension] vs a curvy/twisty/hilly but still-downhill track [extensible faithfully]; (2) stay within real-derby-physics vs allow a playful/arcade second track; (3) same car on both tracks [track-vs-track comparison] vs independent cars; (4) per-side metrics only vs a head-to-head comparison (winner, time delta). A real-loop variant would depend on a 0001-physics-engine extension.
